name: libuhttpd
workload: wrk -t4 -c400 -d10s fetching a small static test.html over localhost from nginx on port 80 and from libuhttpd on port 8080.
claimed_speedup: libuhttpd 281328.83 requests/sec vs nginx 161390.39 requests/sec with identical wrk parameters (about 1.74x, derived from page data); latency avg 2.12 ms vs 3.54 ms.
tradeoffs: Embedded-Linux oriented HTTP/HTTPS server library on libev and http-parser (OpenSSL, mbedtls or wolfssl); CGI, plugins, range requests and nginx-style multi-process model, but far fewer features than nginx.
caveats: README only; no compiler, flags, CPU or kernel stated, nginx version and configuration (worker count, logging) not shown, so tier C. Response sizes differ: nginx run read 385.09 MB for 1,622,012 requests (about 237 bytes each) and libuhttpd run 547.18 MB for 2,826,394 requests (about 194 bytes each), so the servers returned different headers and the comparison is not like for like. Single run, no repeats; the benchmark file test.html is not described. Last commit is a cmake fix in Aug 2025.

name: libwebsockets
workload: uWebSockets author's WebSocket echo-server benchmarks run with default settings: scalability (memory per connection and connection rate, 1M connections for uWebSockets and 500k for the others), short message throughput (10000 connections, 20-byte payload, 10 frames per send) and a 100 MB huge message echo.
claimed_speedup: The page gives only uWebSockets (uWS) ratios: uWS is 11x as lightweight as libwebsockets 2.0 and 63x as lightweight as WebSocket++ v0.7.0; connection performance uWS equal to libwebsockets and 4x WebSocket++; short messages uWS 6x libwebsockets and 3x WebSocket++; huge messages uWS 4x libwebsockets and 2x WebSocket++. Derived from page data: libwebsockets is about 5.7x lighter than WebSocket++ in memory and about 4x faster at connection setup, but about 2x slower than WebSocket++ on short-message and huge-message echo throughput.
tradeoffs: Pure C client and server for http/1, http/2, http/3, websockets, webtransport and MQTT with embedded-friendly footprint; callback-driven API and its own event-loop plumbing (libuv, libevent or libev integration optional), versus websocketpp's header-only C++ with Boost or standalone Asio.
caveats: The numbers are a competitor's table (uWebSockets README, which links benchmark code in its benchmarks/ folder) and libwebsockets and WebSocket++ are never compared directly; the ratios are rounded integers divided against each other, so they are rough. libwebsockets 2.0 (2016) and WebSocket++ 0.7.0 are old versions; hardware, compiler and flags are not stated; the README itself notes the gap to WebSocket++ shrinks from 3x to 2x with one frame per send. Message-throughput result goes against libwebsockets, so only the memory and connection-setup rows support a win. The current libwebsockets README makes no benchmark claims.
